title: Iran Demands Multiple-Entry US Visas for World Cup Squad as Tijuana Base Camp Situation Escalates — No Visas Issued
detail: Iran Football Federation president Mehdi Taj stated on May 28 that the United States must issue multiple-entry visas to the entire Iranian World Cup delegation — players, coaching staff, and medical personnel — because the team will need to cross the US-Mexico border multiple times from their Tijuana, Mexico base camp to attend matches in Los Angeles and Seattle. As of May 28, not a single visa had been issued to any Iranian delegation member despite FIFA president Gianni Infantino's earlier pledge that all players would be able to participate. Iran's group schedule requires at minimum six border crossings: to SoFi Stadium (Inglewood) for June 15 (vs New Zealand) and June 21 (vs Belgium), and to Lumen Field (Seattle) for June 26 (vs Egypt), plus returns. The State Department has not publicly confirmed whether or when multi-entry visas will be issued. FIFA has confirmed the group schedule will not change. The situation represents a legal and logistical flashpoint: Iran's players cannot legally enter the US without visas, yet FIFA insists they will play on US soil. Iran's warm-up friendly vs The Gambia is scheduled for May 29 in Antalya, Turkey — still 14 days from the June 11 tournament opener at Estadio Azteca.

media.caption: Iran demands US issue multiple-entry visas for World Cup squad commuting from Tijuana base camp

title: Champions League Final (PSG vs Arsenal, May 30) — Hakimi Returns to Full Training; Morocco and England Monitor Fitness 14 Days From World Cup
detail: With the UEFA Champions League Final between Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal scheduled for May 30 at Puskás Aréna in Budapest, multiple national teams are monitoring their World Cup players closely. Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi (PSG) returned to full training at Campus PSG after a thigh injury suffered in the semi-final vs Bayern Munich — his participation is now expected, but Morocco will have virtually no recovery window before the group stage. Arsenal's Bukayo Saka (England squad), Declan Rice (England), Gabriel Magalhães (Brazil squad), and Martin Ødegaard (Norway) are all fit for the final. Several squad members face the prospect of playing a Champions League Final and then reporting immediately to World Cup camp. Arsenal's Hakimi counterpart Takehiro Tomiyasu missed the UCL run due to a knee issue but is in Japan's 26-man squad. Real Madrid completed their CL run earlier; the final releases Hakimi to Morocco with fewer than 12 days before the World Cup's opening match. Both teams combined feature at least 11 active World Cup participants from eight nations.

title: Neymar Cleared After Calf Scare — Joins Brazil Camp; Ancelotti Confirms Participation Ahead of Panama Friendly (May 31)
detail: Neymar's minor right calf oedema (2mm) — suffered in a Santos match in the days before the World Cup — has been cleared by Brazil's medical staff, and the 34-year-old forward reported to the Seleção's pre-tournament camp. Santos' medical team had said recovery from the type of oedema typically takes five to ten days, and Neymar publicly dismissed any concerns: 'It's here, all intact.' Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti, who included Neymar in the official 26-man squad announced May 18, confirmed his participation is not in doubt. Brazil face Panama in a farewell friendly at the Maracanã on May 31 before flying to the United States. Neymar last played at a World Cup in 2022 (Qatar) when Brazil were eliminated in the quarterfinals by Croatia on penalties. If fit, the 2026 World Cup represents one of football's most eagerly anticipated redemption arcs. Brazil open Group C vs Morocco at MetLife Stadium on June 13.

media.caption: Neymar clears calf injury scare and joins Brazil's World Cup camp ahead of May 31 farewell friendly vs Panama
